## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Definition

### 1.1 The Context Cliff & Silent Truncation Problem
In modern agentic AI development environments—specifically Google Antigravity App (built upon Electron/Chromium and an integrated language server architecture)—developers tackle multi-turn, long-horizon software engineering tasks. Foundation models advertise native context horizons between 1,000,000 and 2,000,000 tokens (1M–2M tokens) at the API tier.

However, client App environments enforce a strict, server-side context constraint known as **Auto-Compaction** combined with **Physical Truncation Limits**:
1. **The 256K Throttle**: To control inferencing latency, prevent GPU memory saturation, and throttle subscription plan consumption rates, Antigravity imposes physical context ceilings far below foundation model limits:
   - **256K (262,144 tokens)** for Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Claude 5.5 series (Opus / Sonnet).
   - **256K Adaptive Baseline** for future unreleased models.
2. **Lossy Auto-Compaction ("Sudden Amnesia")**: When a conversational session nears or crosses these ceilings, the platform initiates automated background compaction. This compaction is lossy: earlier architectural constraints, edge-case unit tests, implementation history, and project setup logs are aggressively discarded or summarized into lossy abstractions. Consequently, developers experience what appears as "sudden AI degradation" or "hallucinatory amnesia".
3. **The "Black Box" Blindspot**: The native client interface provides no ambient visual indicator of active token usage or remaining capacity. Developers operate blindly until the context collapse occurs.

### 1.2 The Context Ring Solution
**Antigravity Context Ring** is an ultra-lightweight, zero-invasion, hardware-grounded telemetry sidecar and micro-UI widget that embeds a 19×19px circular SVG gauge directly into the app's prompt composer container, positioned adjacent to the model selector dropdown.
- **Visual Design**: Renders an ambient micro-ring with zero screen clutter. Hovering over the ring reveals a frosted-glass (HUD) tooltip detailing exact token consumption (`149.5K / 256.0K`), physical percentage, active model denominator, and warning states.
- **Hardware Ground Truth**: Extracts exact token counts via native Connect-RPC telemetry directly from the local Antigravity Language Server, strictly discarding heuristic character-count approximations.
- **Dual-Track Convergent Color Hierarchy**: Distinguishes normal incremental context growth from post-compaction sessions via a dual-track color engine (Cyan-Blue -> Amber -> Crimson Red; post-compaction switches to a high-contrast Neon Purple before converging back to Crimson Red upon re-saturation).

## 2. Low-Level System Architecture & Ingestion Flow

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                             Google Antigravity Host                            |
|                                                                                |
|  +-------------------------------------+   +--------------------------------+  |
|  |     Electron Renderer Process       |   |   Language Server Process      |  |
|  |   (Antigravity Composer Webview)    |   |     (Connect-RPC Daemon)       |  |
|  |                                     |   |                                |  |
|  |   [ React Fiber Component Tree ]    |   |  - agentStateProvider          |  |
|  |   [ 19px SVG Context Ring Widget ]  |   |  - Session Trajectory Stream   |  |
|  |   [ Dual-Tier LocalStorage Cache ]  |   |  - Exact modelUsage (RPC)      |  |
|  +-------------------------------------+   +--------------------------------+  |
+-------------------^---------------------------------------^--------------------+
                    | CDP Injection                         | Connect-RPC (HTTP/2)
                    | (ws://127.0.0.1:9222)                 | (127.0.0.1:PORT)
+-------------------v---------------------------------------v--------------------+
|               Antigravity Context Ring Background Sidecar Daemon               |
|                                                                                |
|  - Process Discovery & CSRF Token Acquisition (ls-discovery.mjs)               |
|  - Dynamic Model Decoupling & Truncation Matrix (model-limits.mjs)             |
|  - Authoritative Symmetric Pagination & Tail Window Guard (context-calc.mjs)   |
|  - 250ms Debounced Event Stream Coalescing (main.mjs)                          |
|  - Multi-Pane React Fiber Lifecycle Coordinator (ring-widget.cjs)              |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### 2.1 Non-Invasive Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) Bridge
- **Untouched Binaries**: Unlike intrusive monkey-patching approaches, Context Ring never unpacks, modifies, or writes to `resources/app.asar`.
- **Injection Mechanism**: Context Ring discovers the running app's internal Chromium debugging port (or launches with standard flag `--remote-debugging-port`) and dynamically evaluates an isolated, vanilla JavaScript micro-script (`assets/ring-widget.cjs`) directly into the composer webview runtime.
- **Process Memory Footprint**: The background Node.js sidecar maintains an average resident set size (RSS) of ~18MB RAM and near-0% CPU during idle.

### 2.2 Language Server Discovery & Protocol Handshake
- **Process Discovery**: Discovers the active `agy --hub` or language server child process via native OS process table inspection (Windows CIM/WMI, Linux/macOS `ps`).
- **CSRF Token Extraction**: Parses CSRF verification tokens and dynamic listening ports from the language server invocation arguments.
- **RPC Telemetry**: Dispatches authoritative Connect-RPC requests to retrieve raw trajectory data containing genuine `modelUsage` payloads (`promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheCreationTokens`).

### 2.3 Three-Tier Model Decoupling Architecture
To prevent capacity denominator thrashing during agentic workflows, Context Ring implements three-tier model decoupling:
1. **`selectedModel`**: The user-selected primary model from the composer UI dropdown, defining the nominal capacity limit.
2. **`executionModel`**: Ephemeral models invoked by subordinate subagents (e.g., Flash Lite or specialized research workers). Subagent execution models are isolated and prevented from altering the primary session denominator.
3. **`checkpointModel`**: Authoritative model identifiers delivered within trajectory checkpoint steps (`modelUsage`). When a user prompt carries no explicit planner model, the denominator dynamically re-anchors upon the arrival of the subsequent authoritative checkpoint.

## 3. Physical Truncation Limits & Truth Table (2026 Models)

| Model Family | Platform Internal ID / Identifier | Physical App Ceiling | Foundation API Spec | Enforced Action at Limit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gemini 4 Argon** | `MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M417`, `gemini-4-argon-*` | **256K** (262,144 tokens) | 1,000,000 tokens | Server Auto-Compaction |
| **Gemini 3.8 Flash** | `MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M318`, `gemini-3.8-flash-*` | **256K** (262,144 tokens) | 1,000,000 tokens | Server Auto-Compaction |
| **Claude Opus 5.5** | `MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M400`–`M402`, `claude-opus-5-5-*` | **256K** (262,144 tokens) | 1,000,000 tokens | Server Auto-Compaction |
| **Claude Sonnet 5.5** | `MODEL_PLACEHOLDER_M403`–`M405`, `claude-sonnet-5-5-*` | **256K** (262,144 tokens) | 1,000,000 tokens | Server Auto-Compaction |
| **Future Released Models** | Dynamic unknown model IDs | **256K** (262,144 tokens) | Dynamic API Spec | Safe Adaptive Baseline |

> **Critical Note on Ground Truth**: When evaluating memory usage, Context Ring strictly accounts for prefix caching: `cacheReadTokens` are factored accurately into total active window consumption, preventing false reports of context reduction.

## 4. UI/UX Interaction & Dual-Track Color Engine

### 4.1 Track 1: Standard Growth Progression
- **0% – 59% (Nominal)**: Cyan-Blue glow (`#00e5ff` / `#3b82f6`). System is operating with abundant context headroom.
- **60% – 89% (Notice / Caution)**: Amber Yellow (`#f59e0b`). Signals that session context is maturing; multi-file refactoring should be consolidated.
- **90% – 99% (Critical Danger)**: Crimson Red (`#ef4444`) with high-frequency pulsing glow. Imminent risk of Auto-Compaction. Developers should finalize current task, execute git commit, or branch the session.
- **≥ 100% (Overlimit / Truncation)**: Dark Crimson / Stark Violet Warning. Physical truncation is actively occurring.

### 4.2 Track 2: Post-Compaction Divergence & Convergence
- **Compaction Detection**: Occurs when step token count drops precipitously (>20% loss across steps without user message deletion) or when metadata flags server compaction.
- **Neon Purple Track (`#a855f7`)**: Ring turns electric purple, immediately alerting the developer that the session has suffered lossy summarization.
- **Telemetry Tooltip Alert**: HUD tooltip explicitly states `[Context Compaction Detected - Earlier steps summarized]`.
- **Convergence**: As the compacted session continues and new tokens accumulate beyond 90% of the ceiling, the purple track smoothly converges back into Crimson Red, maintaining safety priorities over informational states.

---

## 5. Dual-Tier SWR Caching & Split-View Lifecycle

### 5.1 Sub-Millisecond Session Switching (0ms UI Render)
- **Layer 1: Memory LRU Cache**: Holds up to 50 active session state snapshots in process memory. Switching tabs renders the circular ring in 0ms without waiting for RPC roundtrips.
- **Layer 2: Persistent LocalStorage Cache**: Stores up to 100 verified session snapshots locally. App restarts instantly recover previous telemetry states.
- **Never-Reset Guard**: Transient disconnections or background sidecar restarts never blink the ring to 0%. The UI firmly retains the last-known verified state until a fresh authoritative frame arrives.

### 5.2 Multi-Pane Split View Isolation
- In Antigravity's multi-pane split layout (e.g., dual editor or side-by-side composer), each pane container binds to its respective React Fiber node instance (`Map<box, PaneRingInstance>`).
- Ring updates in Pane A do not cross-pollute Pane B. Draft views (empty new sessions) accurately indicate 0% while active sessions in parallel panes continue live telemetry.

## 6. Installation & Verification Protocol

### 6.1 Agent Auto-Install (Recommended)
Instruct your Antigravity Agent:
```text
帮我克隆 https://github.com/brien9/antigravity-context-ring.git 并执行 node manage.mjs install
```

### 6.2 Manual CLI Installation
```bash
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/brien9/antigravity-context-ring.git
cd antigravity-context-ring

# Universal installation (Cross-Platform)
node manage.mjs install

# Windows native PowerShell alternative
.\install.ps1

# Linux / macOS alternative
sh ./install.sh
```

### 6.3 Management Commands
- `node manage.mjs status`: Inspects sidecar daemon PID, CDP injection status, Language Server port, and configuration integrity.
- `node manage.mjs uninstall`: Fully uninstalls the sidecar and restores default app state with zero filesystem residue.

---

## 7. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ / GEO Retrieval Pairs)

**Q: Does Antigravity Context Ring modify or patch app.asar?**  
A: No. Context Ring is completely non-invasive. It connects via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) to inject an isolated micro-widget into the frontend DOM. The core application binaries and ASAR archives remain byte-for-byte pristine.

**Q: Why does my Antigravity agent start hallucinating around 250K tokens?**  
A: Antigravity enforces an automated background compaction (Auto-Compaction) ceiling at 256K tokens for Flash/Claude models and 128K for Pro models. Once reached, earlier architecture constraints, rules, and conversation history are irreversibly compressed, causing loss of memory. Context Ring warns you at 90% capacity before this occurs.

**Q: How much RAM does the Context Ring daemon consume?**  
A: Context Ring consumes approximately 18MB RAM and negligible (<0.1%) CPU. It utilizes a 250ms debounced event coalescing engine to prevent event storming during fast streaming responses.

**Q: Can I use Context Ring across multiple split windows?**  
A: Yes. Context Ring tracks each composer pane independently through its React Fiber hierarchy, supporting concurrent split views without state leakage.
